title: Man. Post. Cap. X: PLAC — nature’s law binds each for himself; show immediate Adam-act imputation
pass_a_gloss: As for nature’s law: it binds all and each to obedience, but each for himself, and as long as he is. Let something in that law be shown from which Adam’s first actual sin must be immediately imputed to all his posterity.
pass_b_english: But as for the law of nature, it binds all and each to obedience—but each for himself, and as long as he is.
I would like something in that law to be shown me from which it can be proved that the first actual sin of the first man ought to be imputed immediately to all his posterity.
source_text: Ad legem autem naturae quod attinet, obligat omnes & singulos ad obedientiam, sed pro se quemque, & quamdiu est. Ostendi mihi velim aliquid in ea lege, unde probari possit primum primi hominis peccatum actuale omnibus illius posteris imputari debere immediate.

choices.choice: Nature’s law binds each; no immediate Adam-act rule
